subject: Concurrency & latency sampling plan + harness links
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Eli Harper <eli@fastretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concurrency & latency sampling plan + harness links

Thanks for the call this morning, Eli — quick recap and next steps so we can get the qualification run scheduled. High-level ask: we want a single reproducible benchmark that exercises your live traffic shape for both streaming and non-streaming flows. Below are the items we discussed and what we need from your side to proceed.

Summary of targets discussed
- Latency: p50 <= 120ms token-emit for streaming prompt->first-token; p95 <= 300ms for non-streaming first-token for 2k token sequences.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline steady-state of ~200 concurrent user sessions with an expected 3x burst (600) for peak shopping events.
- Streaming requirements: client expects chunked token deltas with sub-200ms inter-chunk latency at low token rates; resumption after intermittent network blips should return within 1s.

What we need from FastRetail (action items)
1) Representative prompt set (we discussed categorical bundles: product-search, upsell-blend, cart-summary) — ideally anonymized JSONL.
2) Traffic sample: 30-min trace or synthetic tps distribution file (we can work from a histogram).
3) Any rate-limiting behavior or client-side timeouts we should mimic (e.g., clients close SSE after X seconds).
4) Preferred window for the run and whether you want our telemetry to include token-level streaming traces (we collect these by default but can redact).

Attachments: sample_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (example prompt shapes), measurement-defs-v1.md (draft of p50/p95 definitions + measurement hooks).

Proposed timeline
- You share items 1–3 by Friday (04/30).
- We stage a harness in our Dedicated QA pool next week and run a 3-hour soak + 10x-burst test.
- Short readout within 48 hours of run with raw metrics + replay artifacts.

If this matches your expectations I'll schedule a 30-min alignment window on Monday to finalise the exact traffic window and credentials.

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 9:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the call this morning, Eli — quick recap and next steps so we can get the qualification run scheduled.

Thanks for the clear recap, Soojin. Confirming we can deliver the following by EOD Friday:
- prompt bundle (anonymized) — attached as traffic_sample_202704.json with 3 labeled buckets (search, upsell, cart).
- sample_config.yaml with our client timeouts and SSE reconnection behavior.

Notes / clarifications:
- Our sessions are sticky per user; concurrency estimate of 200 is peak active sessions, but average concurrent requests (token-generation calls) is closer to 120 during normal commerce hours. We can include a 30-minute window where traffic spikes to ~650 concurrent sessions for Black Friday-style stress validity.
- We log client disconnects after 9s of idle on SSE; if the server does not emit any tokens in that window the client closes. We will include that in sample_config.yaml.

Attaching: traffic_sample_202704.json (7.3 KB), sample_config.yaml (1.1 KB).

Eli Harper

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency & latency sampling plan + harness links

Looping in the bench team notes so we can be ready as soon as FastRetail sends artifacts. Quick operational checklist from our side: 
- We'll use the streaming harness variant v1.8 (KV-cache warmup enabled) and run both quantized and float backends to compare latency tail behavior.
- Tokenization: we need confirmation of the tokenizer version and any pre- or post-processing that alters token boundaries — ask Soojin to capture in the run notes.
- Warmup policy: 5-minute steady warmup at 20% of target TPS, then step to 100% for soak. This matches what we discussed to avoid cold-start tail spikes.
- Measurement definitions: use the measurement-defs-v1.md Soojin shared as authoritative; we'll tag all metrics with run_id and attach replay artifacts to the drive folder.

I'll provision the Dedicated QA pool for a Monday run window (04/30) in region us-west-2. Please confirm if we should enable token-trace capture (adds ~7% overhead) — my recommendation is to enable it for the burst run only.

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

[internal link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folder/1a2B3cHarnessDocs — bench templates and runbook]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Eli Harper <eli@fastretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency & latency sampling plan + harness links

Thanks, Eli — appreciate the fast turnaround. We received the traffic_sample_202704.json and sample_config.yaml and did a quick pass. Two small asks before we finalize the run window:

1) Credentials and endpoint access: please share a short-lived test API key or a sandbox endpoint that mirrors production routing (we only need ingested traffic shape to hit our Dedicated QA pool). If you prefer, we can run the harness against a replay artifact you upload to the shared drive — whichever is quicker.

2) Prompt anonymization: the prompt bundle is good; please remove any PII that might be embedded in free-text fields (user IDs, email addresses). We only need realistic token shapes.

Plan for Monday 04/30 (proposed)
- 08:00–09:00 PT: harness staging and tokenizer alignment check (we'll run a 2-minute smoke to ensure outputs align).
- 09:00–12:00 PT: primary soak (3 hours) + two 10-minute burst windows at 10:30 and 11:30 to hit 650 concurrency.
- 13:00–14:00 PT: quick analysis and readout; deliverables: metrics (p50/p95/p99), token-emit timelines for streaming sessions, and replay artifacts.

If that schedule works, we'll need the shared artifact link and the test key by EOD today so the bench team can pre-stage. I'll drop a short calendar invite once I have confirmation.

Action items (who)
- Eli: share key or upload replay + confirm client disconnect timeout is 9s in the final sample_config.yaml (EOD Fri).
- Karthik: enable token-trace capture for burst window (agreeing to +7% overhead).
- Ben/Monica: prepare run notes and quick troubleshooting playbook for the call during the run.

Thanks — looking forward to a tight run and a clean qualification pass.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
